prompt:
Create one finished opaque flat landscape 16:9 social-media poster advertising a weekend houseplant market. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Input image 1 is our newly authored planning diagram: use its actual-copy anatomy, readable role hierarchy and large image/copy relationships as guidance. It is not finished artwork, a client photograph, or a fixed coordinate requirement. Transform every temporary geometric stand-in into the photographic expression below; all final typography belongs in this native finished image.

Visual design: tactile black-and-white documentary photography, silver highlights, deep charcoal shadows, controlled fine grain and ample midtone detail. Three substantial closely cropped photographic passages occupy the left, together making nearly half the poster and organizing its vertical rhythm. The first shows two anatomically natural bare hands supporting a small houseplant's compact rootball, with a stem visibly connected to living leaves. One palm bears its underside and the other steadies its side. The middle is a tighter material close-up: fingertips gently release loose soil around fine branching roots still connected to that rootball. Show precise ownership of each hand, plausible joints, skin creases, soil particles and physical contact. The bottom pulls back to show a healthy established plant seated stably in a real pot on a working surface, with leaves and stems connected into its soil. Make the crop distances deliberately different and the focus follow contact, not decorative blur. These are observations of plant care, not printed numbered steps or claims of a real person or place. Silver skin and roots recur across the passages; dark soil and pot ground the sequence. Clean intentional photographic boundaries and narrow dark gutters let the three moments read together as a finished single poster.

The right-hand reading column is charcoal with clean light type, adjoining the photographs in one editorial composition. Its story, practical visit and care offer answer the photographic actions. Main Korean Title is immediately recognizable: broad firm modern sans, bold open syllable shapes, clearly dominant weight and breathing space. Keep the market line as a modest eyebrow above it; English name is a small companion below; short Korean sentence is a clear medium-weight Subtitle. The full explanation has mature regular sans letterforms, stable left starts, natural Korean word spaces, calm leading and meaning-led soft lines. Use the guide's paragraph grouping as a starting point, preserving every word. Budget enough body and practical type area to remain comfortably readable at 720px-wide use, not tiny captions. Preserve open Hangul counters, proportional components and even stems; Latin and numerals share compatible optical height and baseline. The paragraph end leads across a short clear gap to the larger regular date, then hours and place, all on its optical left axis. Keep access/care adjacent, then invitation/URL nearby on that same axis. Use harmonious restrained serif numerals for date/hour, with the original en-dashes clearly drawn as long midline bars and clean colons. Do not add spaces within dates, times or URL. Body/footer remain sharply typeset and free of photographic grain.

Grounded, hands-on and trustworthy mood: choosing a plant includes learning how to care for it. The photographs carry substantive caring content and make the image rhythm; do not reduce them to small ornament attached to a passive solid/near-solid/split-field gothic headline/date/information template. Exclude that template and empty-room dressing. No decorative leaf frame, hand icons, pseudo-archival stamps, extra print, invented captions, numbering, logo, QR, watermark, mockup, comparison sheet or extra poster. One flat opaque finished poster only.

Print only these twelve entries, each exactly once, with original Korean/Latin spelling, meaningful word spaces, punctuation, numbers and en-dashes. Soft wrapping may replace word spaces; none of these entries has fixed line breaks:
